meta.title: Netherlands: did Dutch government or Dutch private money reach the key players?
notes: Covers Dutch MFA, Warsaw embassy, Matra/NFRP, Dutch-funded bodies (NHC) and Dutch private funders (Adessium, Stichting Democratie en Media, Vereniging Veronica, Rechters voor Rechters).
'no_link' covers direct payments only; indirect organisational ties are 'fact' edges with tie='indirect' and via=<org>.
Existing node ids reused: hfhr, okopress, watchdog_polska, batory, iustitia, themis, medel, free_courts.
Civitates grants come from a pooled fund; no source attributes a Polish grant to a specific funder, so Dutch shares are unknown.

leads.lead: Dutch government funded the Polish 'coup' players
leads.result: No Dutch government money found to any of the 8 judges, Tusk, Wawrykiewicz, Zurek or Berek, or to Iustitia, Themis, Free Courts, KOD, Akcja Demokracja or Batory. The only Dutch state money found in this network is the Warsaw embassy co-financing HFHR's WATCH DOCS film festival (2017, 2026).
leads.label: no_link

leads.result: Held up as indirect: Adessium (NL) pools money in Civitates, which granted OKO.press EUR 349,888 (2021-24) and Watchdog Polska a 2025 core grant. Other Polish Civitates grantees (not on the map): Panoptykon, Klon/Jawor, OFOP, Association 61, Polish Robert Schuman Foundation, Fundacja Pismo (EUR 300k).
leads.label: fact

leads.lead: Dutch government behind anti-Poland actions (Deputy Justice Minister Marcin Romanowski, Radio Maryja, Dec 2020: 'the Netherlands is an ulcer on the body of the EU')
leads.result: Concerned an Amsterdam court's European Arrest Warrant referral to the CJEU, which OKO.press says he wrongly treated as Dutch government action. Real Dutch state actions were open policy: backing the Commission against Poland at the CJEU (Dec 2020), a parliamentary motion to sue Poland, abstaining on unblocking Poland's recovery funds (2022). None involves money to Polish actors.
